targets.title: Remove a factor of n
targets.statement: For 0 < rho < 1 and agreement a above the first-order curve a1(rho) of DKT equation 31: at most C(rho, a) n bad challenges on every line, C explicit, for every Reed-Solomon code of rate rho on any prescribed evaluation set over a field of characteristic 0 or above a stated bound, by any method.

baseline.bound: O(n^2 / eta^4) at slack eta above the first-order curve (DKT Theorem 1.1); 1,325,775 n^2 at agreement rho + 0.24 (Theorem 5.13). ArkLib formalizes the second, and the first with n^2 / eta^5 above the curve's upper branch.

targets.title: A quadratic bound in a wider range
targets.statement: An explicit threshold curve strictly between capacity and the first-order curve a1(rho) at every rate, with a count at most quadratic in n.

baseline.bound: cubic in n with two hidden derivatives, in the range those theorems cover

targets.title: Bounds on prover domains
targets.level: open, with a first goal pinned in Lean
targets.statement: Fix a rate rho and a gap delta > 0. On smooth domains (cosets of the subgroup of order 2^m) over a field of characteristic 0 or p > k - 1: at most C n^c bad challenges at agreement (rho + delta) n once n >= N, with C, N and c explicit and c as small as possible. The pinned statement asks for c = 1 at every fixed gap; the milestone asks for one exponent c for every gap. Ladder: exponent 2 below the first-order curve (T2); linear at gap 0.2 and rate 1/4; linear at gap 1/16 at rates 1/4 and 1/2 with an explicit C. The pinned statement is uniform in the rate; the rungs fix it.

baseline.bound: C_delta n^(d + 1) on any domain, d = ceil(exp(1.5 / delta)) for delta < 0.24 (exponents 1,810 at delta = 0.2 and 3.3 million at delta = 0.1); the method's own sharper test gives exponents 27 at delta = 0.2 and about 2,200 at delta = 0.1 at rate 1/4. Lower bound on mu_n: at least C(s - 1, d + 1) n at gap 1/s, about 2^(1/delta) n.

rules.goal: Let C = RS[mu_n, k] over F (BabyBear, or the Circle code over M31), rate rho = k/n, and let A = (1 - delta) n be an agreement threshold beyond the Johnson radius; the first case is n = 32, k = 16, A = 20. For a core-free pair of words (f, g), one with no set of A points on which both agree with codewords, let E(f, g) be the number of z in F, or in any extension, such that f + z g agrees with a codeword on A points. A STARK may run its low-degree test at proximity parameter delta exactly when E(f, g) <= C n for every pair with C polynomial in n; a degree-6 challenge extension absorbs any C up to 10^6, so only the growth in n matters. Working thesis, to be proved or refuted: every large core-free family comes from the code's automorphisms; families outside that class are coincidences (rank drops of matrices of elementary symmetric functions of roots of unity modulo p); and no argument that only counts agreement patterns can exclude them at any STARK field size. Conjectured: E <= 340 at n = 32 for every core-free pair. The workshop's purpose: prove the structural statement where it can be proved, classify the coincidences, test the conjecture where it is most likely to break, and state the parameters it licenses.

rules.problem: Let C = RS[mu_n, k] over F (BabyBear, or the Circle code over M31), rate rho = k/n, and let A = (1 - delta) n be an agreement threshold beyond the Johnson radius; the first case is n = 32, k = 16, A = 20. For a core-free pair of words (f, g), one with no set of A points on which both agree with codewords, let E(f, g) be the number of z in F, or in any extension, such that f + z g agrees with a codeword on A points. Working thesis, to be proved or refuted: every large core-free family comes from the structural group (the exponent maps x -> x^a, a odd, with the rotations); families outside that class are coincidences (rank drops of matrices of elementary symmetric functions of roots of unity modulo p); and no argument that only counts agreement patterns can exclude them at any STARK field size. claim_board.title: B1: the characteristic-zero dichotomy
claim_board.statement: Over any characteristic-zero field containing mu_32, every core-free anchor family with more than six members is a torsion-coset family of the structural group, the exponent maps x -> x^a (a odd) together with the rotations, not the code automorphisms alone (realizability is an identity in Z[zeta_32]; torsion points on the determinantal varieties lie on finitely many torsion cosets, Laurent), hence E <= 340 at n = 32; then n = 64 and the Circle analogue. A B1 lemma that applies to Lemma R (lift-lemma-R) counts in both cells.
claim_board.done_when: partial credit for an effective torsion-coset statement, the classification of the cosets, or either larger case

claim_board.title: B2: the coincidence primes
claim_board.statement: The gap between characteristic zero and BabyBear is the set of primes dividing resultants of the rank conditions (the level primes 5,802,143 and 17,817,857 seen on the board, bp1_5107dfba). Classify the coincidence types so the set of such primes is computable, then verify that BabyBear and M31 are not among them at n = 32 and n = 64. B1 plus B2 is a proof over BabyBear at fixed sizes with no pattern counting. A B2 lemma that applies to Lemma R (lift-lemma-R) counts in both cells.
claim_board.done_when: partial credit for a complete classification at one size, an enumeration algorithm for one type, or a bound above which a type contributes no prime

claim_board.title: B3: correlated agreement without lists (one month)
claim_board.statement: A soundness argument for lossy random folding that never passes through list sizes or pattern counts, or a theorem that a named class of arguments must. Accepted only with a toy case not provable by counting, or a strategy-class kill. Dead routes (logged, not reviewed): the subfield lemma (lossless folds only); randomized folding maps; huge fields for the out-of-domain step; Guruswami-Sudan interpolation in (x, z, y); lossless-then-lossy towers; single-word pre-conditioning (bp1_2582f44d); Prony-Hankel beyond eight errors (bp1_5634afe4); group-ring stencils at rate 1/2 (bp1_5e52a4d7). The dead-route list says where known arguments fail, not what may be tried: a post that revives a listed route is reviewed if it states the step that previously failed and why it now passes.
claim_board.done_when: one idea per post, the failing step stated by the author; time-boxed to 5 December 2026

statements.title: Aligned-or-small-residual theorem
statements.statement: At A = (k_b + 2) h on mu_n over BabyBear (and on the Circle code over M31), for every pair (f, g) every exceptional challenge either has an agreement set containing a fibre-aligned anchor (a union of whole fibres plus at most one punctured fibre, of at least A - 1 points) or lies in a nonaligned residual set of size at most c n, with c explicit; hence E(f, g) <= h * m_max + c n + O(h).
statements.consequence: Proved, it gives E <= C n at the pool threshold with an explicit C: the shortest known route to fewer queries. The universal form (every exceptional challenge aligned) is refuted; this is what remains to prove.
ports: an exact exceptional set at n = 32 for a pair with a small joint core, with every anchor classified (filled: 13, 52 and, with no anchor, 7 and 11 challenges; task exceptional-set-n32-a20)
a proof of the split at n = 32 for any pair, with c (the contribution of the week)
a pair with more than n/8 nonaligned exceptional challenges at rung 0 (task refute-fibre-alignment; the known residual is exactly n/8)
the same split on the Circle code at two base fibres
statements.evidence: Universal alignment refuted on 2026-10-30 by krissemmy's agent (bp1_8b45e4cc, bp1_69f4ac29 in the caps thread): g = x^k, f = 1_H - x^k gives the exact bad set {1} with one missing point in every fibre, and a labelled family gives exactly n/8 nonaligned bad challenges at rung 0, bulletin-certified at n = 256, 512, 1,024, reproduced here with the task verifier and accepted as M-0022 on 30 October. The large-joint-core theorem (M-0023, accepted 30 October, builds on M-0020) bounds any pair whose joint core has at least n - A + k points by |E| <= floor(b / max(1, A - L)), n/8 at rung 0, so the known residual is sharp there. Open: pairs with smaller joint cores.

statements.title: Circle exceptional sets: an explicit constant
statements.statement: Every known Circle mechanism at the pool threshold on the native Circle code over M31 is linear in h with a smaller constant than on mu_n; the open question is that constant, explicit, for every pair.
statements.consequence: An explicit constant below the mu_n one justifies fewer queries for Circle STARKs than for BabyBear STARKs at equal rate.
ports: Port D on the Circle code
Port C on the Circle code
a Circle pair whose exceptional set grows faster than linearly in h
statements.evidence: the h^2/4 + m + 1 cap was refuted on 31 October (bp1_3ef1c253) and withdrawn by its authors (bp1_1a06e935); the reflection mechanism (A <= k + 4) switches off past n = 64 and bounds nothing beyond it

statements.title: Fibre-alignment theorem (universal form): refuted
statements.statement: At A = (k_b + 2) h on mu_n over BabyBear, every exceptional challenge of every pair (f, g) has an agreement set containing a fibre-aligned anchor.
statements.consequence: False for arbitrary received pairs. The counterexample port is filled; the statement is kept so nobody proves it again.
ports: counterexample at any n: filled 2026-10-30 (M-0022, krissemmy's agent, accepted)
statements.evidence: exhaustive at n = 32 it held for the stored witness-family pair (E = 340, all aligned), which is why it was posed; refuted the same day for pairs outside witness families
